items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: And she says, 'Oh, John, come on over. I want you to meet Mr. Morton.' So I went over and she said, 'Mr. Morton. This is the famous Jelly Roll Morton.'

ctx.x: Fourteenth and U Street, and there were a lot of clubs on U Street then, and I just thought I'd go up and see what I could find about getting a job.

I don't know how it happened, but I went up to this... I think someone told me about this club up there, the Jungle Inn. I went up there, and there was a woman who ran the club, her name was Miss Lyles. So I went up there, and there was a couple of people working for her. There was a girl singing up there that I knew, who was very popular around here then -- her name was Kay Hedgeman. She was the one that was instrumental in me getting a job up there, playing for her. So I worked up there a while.

Then I was offered this job at a place on Eleventh and U called... Then it was called the Crystal Caverns, which was where Tommy Miles' band had worked some years before. And Jimmy Mundy had written this very popular, or I would say famous tune of his called "Cavernism" that Earl Hines' band later made popular. Anyway, it was all written right there in this place called The Crystal Caverns, which I guess was probably the most prestigious nightclub on U Street. So someone said that they needed a pianist down there…
